verdict.rationale: cubic's own configuration-as-code design makes `cubic.yaml` in the repository root (or an org-level `cubic-config` repo) the source of truth for review behavior and custom agents. Its automation rules therefore live in the codebase and can be versioned, reviewed via PRs and reverted. A community comment confirms the rules are kept in the codebase. However, versioning, review and rollback come from git conventions rather than any documented cubic-native version history or rollback feature, and the docs never describe that workflow explicitly. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of versioning/review/rollback for automations, in-product change history or one-click rollback, and coverage of non-YAML automations such as auto-fix and auto-approval settings.
